chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Rib'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the testimony of a woman who witnessed a man making a will, he said: 'One-quarter of what he willed is valid, according to the value of her testimony.'

As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, who said: Ahmad ibn Hilal wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'A woman testified to a man's will; no one else witnessed it, and among the heirs some believe her and others accuse her.' He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is not unless there is one man and two women, and it is not obligatory that her testimony be executed.'

The resolution in this report is that her testimony is not valid for the entire will, but rather only one man or one man and two women are required for validity. And it does not say that her testimony is invalid for one-quarter of the will, but rather it is compatible with it, and on this basis there is no contradiction between the reports.
ai.seo_question: What is the validity of a woman's testimony in Islamic inheritance and wills according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between the general rule of female testimony being half that of a man (one-quarter share) and the specific requirement for male co-witnesses in wills by distinguishing between partial validity and full execution. This nuanced juristic reasoning ensures that a woman's testimony is not entirely rejected but is limited in scope, reflecting the Shia scholarly approach to harmonizing conflicting narrations in the *Tahdhib*.
